summary: The literal folding/bending sense covers cloth, paper, fingers, back, head and explicit reflexive ruḥe. Body-part possessor and bodily theme should not be inferred solely from German grammatical subject choices.
The existing p.c. examples already mention public humiliation with head lowering and sheep lowering their heads. Their wording and notes are preserved without a new figurative gloss.
The Detransitive newspaper Part. Pass. supplies a folded result property; the boat Infectum-wa describes foldability. Neither occurrence is duplicated.
PrS 9/15 matches the existing PrS 21/1 page reference; retain the inherited reference until the systems are concorded.
At MAC Interview 2/53 does ṭowíwayna mean bending shoots, binding them, or making a carrying bundle? A new technical meaning remains unestablished.

At 65/469 the supplied German says brauchbar and the existing quotation unbrauchbar for the same horse test. Determine the edition reading before changing the entry; the bending sense itself is unaffected.

summary: Wooden rods and vine shoots extend the range of physically manipulated objects. ṭowíwayna may mean folding or bundling; the edition's bind is retained without lexicalizing it as a separate technical operation.
